name: A-low-stop-painted
prompt:
Create one polished portrait-format 2:3 full-body game character illustration, not a collage or concept sheet, no lettering. This is a careful refinement of the supplied adult female archer, preserving her attractive face, athletic natural anatomy, red high ponytail, small gold crest, violet fitted layered costume, sculpted gold armor and ivory-and-gold recurved bow. Maintain the designed fantasy outfit and graceful forceful gesture; the goal is selected visual clarity and correct connected anatomy, not stripping away design. Keep an elegant fitted violet torso garment with coherent seams, a structural waist belt, two clearly attached broad skirt panels, coordinated sculpted shoulder armor, forearm guards and articulated knee/shin armor. Concentrate the gold motif at crest, armor, waist clasp and bow; give the armor thickness and articulated joints. Fabrics have a few broad directional folds. Keep red hair in substantial flowing groups with a handful of loose strands. Natural adult proportions and a visible continuous ribcage-waist-pelvis connection; exactly two arms, two legs, anatomically articulated hands. Costume must follow the anatomy; knee armor covers the actual knee, both legs emerge from the two sides of the pelvis. Keep modest cinematic perspective, dynamic but legible. Preserve enough detail and shading in the face, hands, joints and materials. No plain generic uniform, no excessive ribbons, no wire-thin decorative straps covering the body, no mirror-polished skin, no confetti or huge glowing effects. Entire character, both feet and whole bow contained in frame, with a little breathing room.
REFERENCE ROLES: First image is the edit target and main pose/character reference (the low sliding archer); preserve her low stop, direction of aim and balanced gesture. Second image is the primary PAINTING STYLE reference: confident broad angular brush planes, matte gold planes, intentional edge hierarchy. Third is only a clarity reference for organized color groups and readable face; do not use its pose.
POSE: low lateral sliding stop while aiming to image right. Pelvis low and behind the forward knee; forward leg projects toward lower right with its sole clearly braced on the ground, a moderately enlarged near boot. Other leg bent and folded to image left with knee and rear foot visibly accounted for. Clearly show the front thigh-to-knee-to-shin turn and rear leg chain, with cloth behind them. Upper body remains tall enough between pelvis and shoulders; head aligned toward arrow. Bow hand holds the grip with believable finger articulation. Drawing hand beside jaw, wrist straight and three curled fingertips visibly hook the bowstring beside the arrow nock. The arrow nock and both string segments meet at that same draw point. One straight arrow runs from there through the bow's arrow rest just above the grip toward image right. String connects to the upper and lower bow tips, no extra string. Preserve the tension of the original pose.
PAINTING: strong designed shape language and large connected shadows as in second reference, restrained visible brushwork, dimensional skin turns at shoulder/elbow/knee, crisp face and hands, rich violet against warm muted gold and vivid red hair. Choose edges, don't outline every plane. Restrained pale cool ruined stone silhouettes behind her, angled stone ground and a small dust sweep near feet communicating deceleration. The figure dominates. This is a detailed finished painting with simplified mark-making, not a flat poster silhouette.
